question: My checkout flow has 11 steps. Can I put all of them into one funnel?
reference_answer: No, funnels are limited to 8 steps. If your flow is longer, split it into two funnels at a logical midpoint and compare the completion rates to find the bigger drop-off.
key_facts: Funnels are limited to 8 steps
Split longer flows into two funnels at a logical midpoint
answer: Funnels are limited to a maximum of 8 steps [1]. If your flow is longer, you can split it into two funnels at a logical midpoint [1].

question: on the old v1 stats api, how do i get more than 1000 results from a breakdown?

question: my shopify storefront is tracked fine but checkout and thank you page visits dont show up. why?
reference_answer: Shopify doesn't load your theme on the checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them. You need to add a custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events, which tracks checkout pages and events like add to cart and purchase with revenue.
key_facts: Shopify doesn't load the theme on checkout and Thank you pages
Use a custom pixel in Customer events to track them
answer: Shopify does not load your theme on checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet cannot see them [1]. To track checkout pages and shopping events, you need to add a Plausible custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events [1].

citations.quote: Shopify doesn't load your theme on checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them.
A custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events tracks checkout pages and Shopify's built-in shopping events (add to cart, checkout, purchase) with revenue.

evidence.title: Shopify ecommerce tracking
evidence.text:
Here's how to add Plausible Analytics to your Shopify store and track add to cart, checkout, purchases, revenue and more.

There are two parts:

1. **Your Plausible snippet in your theme** tracks your storefront: home, collection, product and cart pages.
2. **A custom pixel in Shopify's Customer events** tracks checkout pages and Shopify's built-in shopping events (add to cart, checkout, purchase) with revenue. Shopify doesn't load your theme on checkout and Thank you pages, so the theme snippet can't see them.

Note: Moving from Additional scripts or checkout.liquid?
Shopify has switched off Additional scripts and checkout.liquid customizations on the Thank you and Order status pages: on 28 August 2025 for Shopify Plus stores and on 26 August 2026 for all other plans. If you had Plausible code there, it no longer runs. Use the custom pixel below instead.

## Add the Plausible snippet to your theme

* In your Shopify admin, go to **Online Store → Themes**.
* Click the **⋯** button next to your current theme and choose **Edit code**.

Add Plausible to Shopify

* In the **Layout** folder, open **theme.liquid** and paste your Plausible snippet just before the closing `</head>` tag. Your snippet is in the **Site Installation** area of the **General** section in your site settings.
* Click **Save**.

## Add a Plausible custom pixel for checkout and shopping events

* In your Shopify admin, go to **Settings → Customer events**.

Shopify Settings

* Click **Add custom pixel** and name it, e.g. **Plausible**.
* Choose the **Customer privacy** settings (see below).
* Paste the code into the **Code** box: the setup block first, then the blocks for what you want to track.
* Click **Save**, then **Connect**.

question: im switching from a hardcoded plausible snippet to google tag manager. will i get double pageviews, and will i lose my old data?

evidence.title: How the free trial works
evidence.text:
Every Plausible account starts with a free 30-day trial. During the trial you have access to all Business plan features and limits, so you can explore the full product before choosing a plan.

## No credit card, no automatic charges

We don't ask for a credit card when you register. There's no payment method on file, so we can't charge you. Your trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically.

This also means there's nothing to cancel. If you don't want to continue after the trial, you don't need to do anything.

## What happens when the trial ends

If you haven't subscribed by the end of the trial, your dashboard is locked. You can still log in to your account.

We don't keep your website analytics data indefinitely after your trial ends.

If you don't subscribe, we'll stop collecting new stats and eventually delete your dashboards and all their stats permanently. We'll email you before deletion so you have time to subscribe or export your stats.

After your trial ends, we keep recording stats for a few more days, and the email we send when the trial expires says how many. Recording stops at midnight UTC on the last of those days.

Automatic deletion removes your sites and stats, but your login stays until you delete your account.

Subscribe before deletion to unlock your dashboards and keep your historical stats. Deleted stats cannot be recovered.

## Delete your account at any time

You can delete your account with a few clicks at any point, during or after the trial. Go to **Account settings**, scroll to the **Danger zone** section and click **Delete Account**. This removes all your sites and collected stats.

To start a new 30-day trial, delete your account and sign up again with the same email.

question: how can i get hourly vistor numbers and still see the hours where nobdy visited? my graph has gaps
reference_answer: Use the time:hour dimension to group by hour. Hours with no data aren't returned, so also set include.time_labels to true, which requires a time dimension and adds meta.time_labels with all the labels valid for your date_range so you can fill the gaps.
